clue.text: Very nasty about brother or sister being seen

indicators.note: the word for very nasty wraps itself around the sibling, so it sits about it

parts.note: vile means very nasty
a sib is a sibling, a brother or sister

explanation.surface: Someone nasty is caught out treating a sibling badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' in the surface, but it is the container signal; 'being seen' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in plain view, able to be noticed by the eye, is visible.

clue.text: Company find new worker to whom secrets can be entrusted

definitions.text: to whom secrets can be entrusted

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of find are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A firm recruits a fresh employee who can be trusted with confidential matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the four letters of 'find'; the worker is the insect, not an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusted friend who keeps private matters safe is a confidant.

clue.text: Daughter following scent pried around

indicators.note: the daughter's letter comes after, following, the scent word

parts.note: nose can mean a scent or bouquet, as of wine
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A girl tracks a smell and goes snooping about.
explanation.definitionFit: To snoop or poke about in others' business is to have nosed around.

clue.text: Oxford University getting in new amenity? Whatever is required

indicators.note: the university's letters get into the reworked amenity letters
new signals that the letters of amenity are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oxford acquires a new facility, asking whether that is everything wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges 'amenity' and 'getting in' sets the university's letters just after its first letter; the question mark flags the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase offers anything at all that one could ask for, an idiom of unlimited choice.

clue.text: Competition with artist? Just a little

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's stock artist
a trace is just a little of something

explanation.surface: Asked whether a contest involves a painter, someone replies that it does slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the fierce competitive struggle of working life, an idiom.

clue.text: Go on horse round German hill-range

indicators.note: the riding word goes round the German letter

parts.note: to ride is to go on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider travels on horseback around a German upland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts G inside RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow elevated crest of land is a ridge.

clue.text: Knot made by leader in Istanbul for pub?

definitions.meaning: a decorative ornamental knot in rope, shaped like a turban
the head of a Turk, a common English pub name

explanation.surface: A knot is apparently tied by an Istanbul chief to serve as a pub's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link; the second reading takes 'leader' as a head, the head of a man from Istanbul, and pubs are often called after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The turban-shaped rope knot and the pub sign both bear the same name.

clue.text: It's potential gain to get line put in correct orientation

indicators.note: the reworked gain letters get, receive, the line letter inside them
potential suggests the letters of gain could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A possible gain is spelled out for getting a line straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' turns GAIN into AIGN, and 'to get' puts L inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: To set things straight in proper relative positions is to align them.

clue.text: European no-good country? Most Britons wouldn't agree!

definitions.text: European no-good country? Most Britons wouldn't agree!

parts.note: NG is the abbreviation for no good
land means a country, a nation

explanation.surface: Someone calls a European nation worthless, and the British would object.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a jibe at a European country; the wordplay E + NG + LAND builds it, and the closing remark is the setter's joke that the British would dispute the label.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's dismissive description points to the British nation itself, which most British residents would hardly call worthless.

clue.text: French writer's getting deserts

definitions.meaning: George Sand, French novelist, with the possessive

explanation.surface: A French author is getting what she deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; 'deserts' is read as arid places, not just deserts.
explanation.definitionFit: George Sand was the pen name of a French novelist, and desert regions are expanses of sand.

clue.text: Unimportant person responsible to Heather?

parts.note: under, as in serving under a boss, means answerable to
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A minor person seems to report to a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a boss's name, but it is the plant: LING is a heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate of low rank is an underling.

clue.text: Debt Linda wiped out meeting unknown male?

indicators.note: wiped out suggests destruction, so these letters are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Linda's debts are cleared as she goes to meet a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wiped out' rearranges DEBT LINDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic engagement arranged with someone not seen before is a blind date.

clue.text: Woman and boy beside main road, reversing

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: reversing turns the road's letters backwards

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's main north-south road, with 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A woman and her son are beside a highway, reversing a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the Great North Road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is taken as letter I, and 'reversing' gives IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a female forename.

clue.text: Praise lieutenant after returning chopper

indicators.note: the lieutenant's letters follow after the other piece
returning means the word for chopper comes back, read backwards

parts.note: an axe is a chopper

explanation.surface: An officer is commended once the helicopter comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: Chopper looks like a helicopter, but it is an axe; 'returning' gives EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify or extol someone is to praise them.

clue.text: Take vital mixture that's gassy?

indicators.note: mixture signals a blend, so these letters are stirred together anew

explanation.surface: Someone takes an essential medicine, apparently a fizzy one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges TAKE VITAL. Gassy here means chatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Gassy is slang for chatty, full of talk.

clue.text: European cited about measure describing Faberge work?

indicators.note: the word for cited goes about the measure

parts.note: named means cited, mentioned
an ell is an old cloth measure

explanation.surface: A European mentioned a measurement concerning a Fabergé egg.
explanation.walkthrough: An ell is an old cloth length of about 45 inches; Fabergé is famed for jewelled, coated eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabergé eggs are famous for their glossy coloured vitreous coatings, so the work is enamelled.

clue.text: Woman's language hard to ignore in state capital

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name

indicators.note: to ignore means the hard letter is left out of the language word

parts.note: Polish is a language
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A woman's speech in a state capital drops its harder sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' removes H from POLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapolis is the capital of Maryland in the US.

clue.text: Solitary German ousting English drinking gin wistfully?

indicators.note: drinking means the altered word takes in the spirit
ousting means the German letter replaces the English one

parts.note: lonely means solitary

explanation.surface: A lonely German pushes out an Englishman and drinks gin with yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting' swaps the English letter for the German one to give LONGLY, and 'drinking' takes the spirit inside; the question mark softens the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking with yearning or desire is looking wistfully.

clue.text: Language of tardy Mediterranean type?

parts.note: late means tardy
a Latin is a person from southern Europe

explanation.surface: Someone asks which tongue a sluggish southern European speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Late Latin is the form of the old Roman tongue used in late antiquity.

clue.text: A match for Satan

explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is both an old friction match and a name for the Devil.

clue.text: Dog's energy when chasing racket

indicators.note: when chasing means the energy piece comes behind the racket piece

parts.note: a din is a racket, a loud noise
go means energy, vigour

explanation.surface: A dog shows its energy when chasing a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog's here reads as 'Dog is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia.

clue.text: Start poetically with feature of South Africa which is to be worked on

definitions.text: which is to be worked on

parts.note: ope is a poetic form of open, to start
the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A poet begins with a South African motif.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths, the quantity an operation acts on is the operand.

clue.text: Copper's very quiet taking a drink

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
pp, pianissimo, is very quiet in music

explanation.surface: A police officer is quiet while having a tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman, but it is the metal, symbol CU. A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a cup of tea, a hot beverage.

clue.text: Get nut from tin after exercise

indicators.note: after puts the tin piece behind the exercise piece

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: After a workout someone opens a tin for a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is an American hickory nut.

clue.text: European parliamentarian taking care in formulating drug

parts.note: MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

indicators.note: formulating suggests composing, so these letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: An MEP is careful when drafting drug laws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formulating' rearranges CARE IN to ACRINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mepacrine is an antimalarial medicine.

clue.text: Old King of Crete has lad I'm to raise

indicators.note: in a down clue, to raise means these pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a son is a lad
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The legendary Cretan king has a boy he means to bring up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to raise' turns SON IM upwards, as in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Minos was the legendary ruler of Crete in Greek myth.

clue.text: Drink like a fish when in credit?

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the credit letters

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: One drinks like a fish when one has money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink like a fish' looks like the idiom; 'Drink' alone is the definition and 'like' a link. The ide is a European freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is an alcoholic beverage made from apples.

clue.text: Dissident left on island after the truth

indicators.note: after puts the island behind the truth word
on, in an across clue, puts the left letter after the island

parts.note: a fact is the truth
Iona is a Scottish island

explanation.surface: A dissenter leaves for an island after the facts come out.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a Hebridean island off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a splinter group, dissenting from the main body, is factional.

clue.text: Pester mother with principle

parts.note: to dog is to pester, follow persistently
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Someone pesters their mother on a point of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A firmly held doctrine or tenet is a dogma.

clue.text: Right to annoy second soccer team in Scotland

parts.note: anger means to annoy

explanation.surface: It is fine to provoke the second club of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Glasgow football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is a Glasgow football club.

clue.text: Went out of way, with support, to suppress resistance

indicators.note: to suppress means the supported word holds down the resistance letter inside it

parts.note: stayed means supported, held up with stays
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off course, supported, to quell opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suppress' puts R inside STAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander from the proper path is to have strayed.
